findings.issue: Rating range check is a logical no-op: a value cannot simultaneously be <1 and >5, so no value is ever rejected by the range portion of the condition.
findings.evidence: if (!Number.isInteger(rating) || (rating < 1 && rating > 5)) — e.g. rating=0 or rating=999 (integers) pass validation and are persisted via Review.updateReview(reviewId, { rating }).

findings.issue: Pagination offset is off by one page: uses page*pageSize instead of (page-1)*pageSize, per the function's own doc comment stating 'page starts at 1'.
findings.evidence: return all(`SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY ${column}, id LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`, [pageSize, page * pageSize]) — getBooksPage(1, 10) skips the first 10 rows and returns rows 11-20 instead of 1-10.

findings.issue: User-controlled sort string is interpolated directly into the SQL ORDER BY clause with no whitelist/validation, allowing SQL injection.
findings.evidence: ORDER BY ${sort} in getReviewsSorted, called from src/routes/api.ts with const sort = (req.query.sort as string) || 'r.created_at DESC'; passed straight through with no validation, unlike getBooksPage which validates sortKey against BOOK_SORT_COLUMNS.

findings.issue: Review display_name is inserted into HTML response without escaping, allowing stored XSS.
findings.evidence: `${top.display_name} rated it ${top.rating}/5` sent via res.send with raw template interpolation; display_name is user-supplied via POST /users with no sanitization at creation or render time.
